French borrowing costs reach 24-year high amid budget and unrest fears

France's 10-year government bond yields have surpassed 5%, reaching their highest level since 2002, a 24-year high. This increase in borrowing costs is attributed to concerns over the government's failure to pass a budget and the fallout from civil unrest. The yield on these bonds has climbed above 5% amid political concerns and the delayed budget.
